**Working Principle:** UV-Vis spectroscopy is based on the absorption of ultraviolet or visible radiation (200–800 nm) by molecules, causing electronic transitions from occupied molecular orbitals (HOMO: $\sigma$, $\pi$, $n$) to unoccupied molecular orbitals (LUMO: $\sigma^*$, $\pi^*$).

**Interpretation for Bond Identification:**
* $\sigma \rightarrow \sigma^*$ transitions occur in saturated compounds (e.g., alkanes) requiring high energy (vacuum UV).
* $n \rightarrow \sigma^*$ transitions occur in saturated compounds with heteroatoms ($-OH$, $-NH_2$, $-X$).
* $\pi \rightarrow \pi^*$ and $n \rightarrow \pi^*$ transitions occur in unsaturated systems (alkenes, carbonyls, aromatic rings), identifying double bonds, triple bonds, and conjugated systems via specific $\lambda_{max}$ values.
proTip: Keep the electronic transition energy order in mind: $\sigma \rightarrow \sigma^* > n \rightarrow \sigma^* \approx \pi \rightarrow \pi^* > n \rightarrow \pi^*$.
